papers.title: The washing fraction: An overlooked source of molecular information obtained during SPME experiment.
papers.authors: Treder N, Zhu X, Leszczyńska D, Bo T, Kwok T, Pawliszyn J
papers.abstract:
The molecular processes occurring at the interface between biocompatible solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coatings and biological tissue remain poorly understood. The routine post-extraction washing step provides an opportunity to recover and characterize molecules associated with this interface before analytes retained in the extraction phase are desorbed.
In this study, washing fractions generated after 30 min of extraction from bovine skeletal-muscle tissue slices using acupuncture-needle SPME probes coated with C18, self-wettable HLB (wHLB), weak anion-exchange (WAX), or phenylboronic acid (PBA) phases were analyzed by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing with UV and mass spectrometric detection (icIEF-UV/MS) for intact-protein profiling and by liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) for metabolomic and lipidomic profiling. Protein analysis revealed several putative skeletal-muscle protein matches in washing fractions obtained with both WAX and PBA coatings, despite their distinct extraction chemistries, demonstrating coating-dependent recovery of tissue-derived proteins during washing. Washing multiple needles in a fixed volume increased the number of detected intact protein masses, improving protein-profile coverage. Metabolomic and lipidomic profiling revealed coating-dependent differences in the distributions of molecular features between the washing and desorption fractions, demonstrating their distinct molecular compositions. In particular, for C18-coated probes, the washing fraction provided complementary information on relatively polar molecular features that were weakly represented or absent in the corresponding desorption fraction.
These findings establish the routinely discarded SPME washing fraction as an additional source of molecular information complementary to conventional desorption. Analysis of both fractions may therefore expand molecular coverage from a single sampling event without requiring additional tissue sampling.

papers.title: Acupuncture Integration in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS): A Comprehensive Evidence-Based Review.
papers.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
papers.authors: Yang W, Xu J, Yan Q, Xu W, Zheng Y
papers.abstract: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols have significantly improved perioperative outcomes; however, challenges including opioid-related adverse effects, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), delayed gastrointestinal recovery, and chronic post-surgical pain remain incompletely resolved. These limitations are closely linked to perioperative neuroimmune and autonomic dysregulation, which current pharmacologic strategies do not adequately address. This review examines acupuncture and acupoint-based stimulation modalities, including electroacupuncture and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation, as adjunctive interventions within ERAS pathways. Current evidence suggests that these modalities may reduce postoperative pain and opioid consumption, decrease PONV incidence, and support gastrointestinal recovery in selected perioperative settings, with generally acceptable safety when delivered by trained practitioners. Mechanistic investigations suggest that these effects may involve modulation of spinal nociceptive processing, vagal anti-inflammatory pathways, and autonomic balance. Despite heterogeneity in study design and intervention protocols, the cumulative evidence supports the potential role of acupuncture as an adjunctive perioperative strategy, particularly for PONV and selected recovery outcomes. Acupuncture may serve as a mechanism-informed adjunct within ERAS pathways, with stronger conclusions requiring large, high-quality randomized controlled trials using standardized protocols and clinically meaningful endpoints.

papers.title: Rapid screening and identification of epigallocatechin-3-gallate and quercetin derived from traditional Chinese medicine as inhibitors of pan-orthopoxviruses : Quercetin and EGCG against orthopoxviruses.
papers.authors: Sun J, Huang B, Ye F, Huo S, Wang M, Zhao L et al.
papers.abstract: Poxviruses are major zoonotic pathogens. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has been used for antiviral treatment; however, data on the efficacy of TCM against poxviruses remain limited. Therefore, this study assessed the antiviral activity of 15 active ingredients derived from TCM against orthopoxviruses. The cytotoxic concentration 50 (CC50) was determined using Vero cells. Subsequent screening was performed to select compounds with potential antiviral activity in vitro using vaccinia virus expressing green fluorescent protein (VTT-EGFP) as a model. (-)-Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), NK007, quercetin, emetine, and pyrvinium pamoate demonstrated notable anti-orthopoxvirus activity in Vero cells. The EC50 value of quercetin and EGCG were 3.04-8.00 µM and 39.39-60.55 µM, respectively by qPCR and 1.24-2.53 µM and 44.76-66.36 µM by Plaque assay in Vero cells infected with orthopoxviruses (VTT-EGFP, ectromelia virus, and monkeypox virus), respectively. Quercetin primarily targeted the post-entry phase, whereas EGCG affected the viral entry phase. Quercetin and EGCG suppressed the transcription of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1 and IL-6, and when combined with the antiviral drug cidofovir (CDV), exerted a synergistic antiviral effects against VTT-EGFP. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance analyses revealed the EGCG-binding affinity and conserved interactions with VACV A27L and D8L proteins. Quercetin and EGCG effectively inhibited viral replication and suppressed the expression of inflammatory cytokines in Vero cells infected with orthopoxvirus. Furthermore, EGCG exhibited binding affinity and conserved interactions with VACV A27L and D8L proteins in vitro. These findings will facilitate the development of therapeutic agents that act against monkeypox as well as infection with other orthopoxviruses.

papers.title: Herbal Medicine in Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Lyu S, Li J, Wan JY, Zhang Q, Yao H et al.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the most common chronic diseases, affecting 537 million adults worldwide, a number projected to rise to 783 million by 2045. Single-target agents lower glucose but act weakly on the inflammatory, oxidative and microbial features driving residual complication risk. Chinese herbal medicine addresses this limitation. This review summarizes current evidence on Chinese herbal medicine in the prevention and treatment of T2DM, covering single herbs, active constituents and classic formulas. Herbal medicines and constituents act simultaneously on insulin signaling, inflammation, oxidative stress and the gut microbiota, a profile matching the multifactorial pathophysiology of T2DM and complementing current pharmacotherapy. Added to standard therapy, herbal interventions improve glycemia, insulin resistance and β-cell function, and slow progression from prediabetes to diabetes, with a low incidence of hypoglycemia. Single herbs (Coptis chinensis, Panax ginseng, Pueraria lobata), active constituents (berberine, puerarin, quercetin, baicalin, ginsenoside Rb1), and classic formulas (Ge-Gen-Qin-Lian Decoction, Liu-Wei-Di-Huang Pill) activate AMPK and PI3K/Akt-GLUT4 signaling, preserve β-cell identity and survival, and remodel the gut microbiota and bile acid pool. The gut is a recurrent upstream site of action, so that the low oral bioavailability of several constituents is part of the mechanism rather than a limitation. Mechanistic evidence remains predominantly preclinical, batch variability limits reproducibility, and no trial reviewed here reports cardiovascular or renal hard endpoints. Chinese herbal medicine represents a promising adjunct to standard type 2 diabetes care, offering a mechanistic breadth that addresses residual complication risks. To validate these broader metabolic benefits, future clinical trials must evaluate its efficacy against definitive clinical endpoints.

papers.title: Zishen Yutai Pill antagonizes age-related ovarian hypofunction and infertility by regulating mitochondrial function.
papers.authors: Luo Z, Wei J, Xu N, Ai Y, Zhang Q, Luo H et al.
papers.abstract: Age-related decline in ovarian function is a major cause of female infertility, yet effective interventions remain limited. Zishen Yutai Pill (ZYP) is a well-established traditional Chinese herbal formula widely used in assisted reproduction; however, its effects on age-associated ovarian decline and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a small prospective pilot cohort of women undergoing assisted reproductive treatment, ZYP was associated with higher mature oocyte (93.89% vs. 86.13%, P = 0.046) and clinical pregnancy rates (73.33% vs. 27.27%, P = 0.045). Motivated by these preliminary observations, we established aged-related ovarian changes in mice, identified 28 weeks of age as the onset of ovarian functional decline, and subsequently investigated the effects and underlying mechanisms of ZYP in this model. ZYP improved ovarian reserve, endocrine function, oocyte quality, and fertility outcomes in aged mice. These benefits were associated with enhanced mitochondrial function in oocytes, including improved mitochondrial distribution and membrane potential, increased mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) transcription, reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and increased expression of the mitochondrial fusion proteins OPA1 and MFN1. Together, our clinical and animal findings indicate that ZYP may improve ovarian reserve and oocyte quality, potentially through the regulation of mitochondrial function, thereby providing a potential strategy for alleviating age-related ovarian decline and infertility.

papers.title: [Frequently asked questions in data mining research papers on acupuncture literature].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Li J, Xu J
papers.abstract: Data mining has become a widely used method in acupuncture literature research in recent years. This paper summarizes common problems in data mining research papers on acupuncture literature, including unreasonable research purposes, insufficient methodological rigor, uneven quality of original literature, and inadequate in-depth analysis of results. From the perspective of improving the practical value of such papers, suggestions are put forward for research topic selection and paper writing, such as clarifying practical clinical problems to be solved, standardizing the design, implementation and reporting of acupuncture clinical trials, improving the quality of original literature, and scientifically analyzing mining results. It is expected to enhance the application efficiency of data mining in acupuncture literature research and the practical value of such studies.

papers.title: [Research progress on the mechanism of acupuncture in protecting the intestinal barrier to intervene in Parkinson's disease].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Shen X, Shi J, Zhu Y, Zhang X, Wu H, Cui H
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence from recent years indicates a strong association between PD pathogenesis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, with impairment of the intestinal barrier being recognized as a critical initiating factor. This review summarizes current research on the multi-target mechanisms through which acupuncture protects the intestinal barrier and thereby intervenes in PD progression. Evidence suggests that acupuncture can restore gut microbiota homeostasis by increasing short-chain fatty acids and reducing lipopolysaccharide levels; upregulate the expression of tight junction proteins (zonula occludens-1, occludin) and mucin (Muc 2), thereby directly reinforcing the intestinal physical barrier; effectively clear aberrant α-Syn aggregates in the colon and suppress the NOD-like receptor 3 and nuclear factor κB pathway to alleviate intestinal inflammation. These mechanisms act synergistically to maintain intestinal barrier integrity and block the transmission of pathological signals from the gut to the brain.

papers.title: [Research progress on the neuro-endocrine-immune regulatory mechanism of acupuncture in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Xie W, Wang Y, Li L, Zhao Y, Wei Y, Yan X
papers.abstract: Acupuncture can effectively improve cognitive function and delay disease progression in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Studies have shown that acupuncture treatment for AD is closely related to the effective regulation of the neuro-endocrine-immune (NEI) network. This article reviews the NEI mechanism of acupuncture in the treatment of AD mainly from the following aspects: benign regulation of the nervous system--regulating levels of central neurotransmitters (cholinergic, monoaminergic, amino acid, neuropeptide) and their receptors, brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels, and regulation of neuronal cell cycle re-entry; regulation of the endocrine system--ameliorating hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction, regulating levels of related hormones (estrogen, testosterone) and insulin-like growth factor-1; regulation of the immune system--modulating activation of central neuroimmune cells (microglia, astrocytes) and homeostasis of the peripheral immune system, and regulating related inflammatory signaling pathways (such as Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor-κB, Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B, etc.). This article aims to provide a basis for further exploring the mechanism and clinical applications of acupuncture in the treatment of AD.

papers.title: [Mechanism study of acupuncture regulating inflammatory response and apoptosis via the MEK/ERK pathway to improve premature ovarian insufficiency].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Guo L, Wu X, Hao J, Chang B, Liu L
papers.abstract:
To explore the mechanism of acupuncture in improving ovarian function in rats with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) by regulating the inflammatory response and apoptosis via the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) pathway.
SD rats were randomly divided into blank, POI and acupuncture groups, with 15 rats in each group. The POI model was established by intraperitoneal injection of cyclophosphamide for 15 consecutive days. Rats in the acupuncture group received acupuncture at "Guanyuan" (CV4) and bilateral "Sanyinjiao" (SP6) for 30 min, once daily for 3 weeks. The estrous cycle of rats was observed. Body weight and ovarian wet weight were measured, and the ovarian index was calculated. Ovarian histopathology was observed after HE staining, and follicles at different stages were counted. The serum contents of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), estradiol (E2), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-10, and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and the ovarian contents of IL-1β, IL-10, and TNF-α, were detected by ELISA. The apoptosis level of granulosa cells was assessed by flow cytometry. The mRNA expressions of MEK1/2, ERK1/2, Bcl-2 associated X protein (Bax), B-cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2), nuclear factor-κB p65 (NF-κB p65), and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in the ovary were detected by qPCR. The protein expressions of phosphorylated (p)- MEK1/2, MEK1/2, p-ERK1/2, ERK1/2, Bax, Bcl-2, NF-κB p65, and COX-2 were detected by Western blot. Immunofluorescence was used to detect the expression of p-ERK1/2 protein in ovarian tissue.
Compared with the blank group, the POI group showed an increased disorder rate of the estrous cycle (P<0.01), and decreased body weight, ovarian wet weight, and ovarian index (P<0.01);disordered ovarian pathological structure, decreased numbers of primordial, primary, secondary, and mature follicles (P<0.01), and increased number of atretic follicles (P<0.01). Additionally, the contents of serum FSH, IL-1β, and TNF-α, as well as ovarian IL-1β and TNF-α were increased (P<0.01), whereas the contents of serum AMH, E2, IL-10, and ovarian IL-10 were decreased (P<0.01). The apoptosis level of granulosa cells was elevated (P<0.01). The mRNA expressions of MEK1/2, ERK1/2, Bax, NF-κB p65 and COX-2 in the ovary were increased (P<0.01), while Bcl-2 mRNA expression was decreased (P<0.01). The protein expressions of p-MEK1/2, p-ERK1/2, Bax, NF-κB p65 and COX-2 were increased (P<0.01), while Bcl-2 protein expression was decreased (P<0.01). The immunofluorescence intensity of p-ERK1/2 in the ovary was enhanced (P<0.01). Compared with the POI group, all the above indicators were significantly reversed in the acupuncture group (P<0.01, P<0.05).
Acupuncture can improve ovarian function in POI rats. The mechanism may be related to regulating the MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby alleviating ovarian inflammatory response and inhibiting granulosa cell apoptosis.

papers.title: [Effect of moxibustion at "Guanyuan" (CV4) on mitochondrial iron metabolism in spinal cord tissue of rats with urinary retention after spinal cord injury].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Duan S, Bai C, Yang S, Lu R, Gao J, Liu C
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of moxibustion at "Guanyuan" (CV4) on urodynamics and mitochondrial iron metabolism in spinal cord tissue of rats with urinary retention after spinal cord injury (SCI), investigate the mechanism of moxibustion in treating urinary retention after spinal cord injury.
Forty-four Wistar rats were randomly divided into a sham operation group (n=12) and a modeling group (n=32). The urinary retention model after SCI was established using Allen's weight-drop method in the modeling group. Twenty-four successfully modeled rats were then randomly divided into a model group (n=12) and a moxibustion group (n=12). Rats in the moxibustion group received moxibustion at CV4 for 15 min, once daily for 14 consecutive days. After the intervention, urodynamic parameters including bladder maximum capacity, bladder leak point pressure, and bladder compliance were measured. HE staining was used to observe the morphology of the injured spinal cord segment. The ultrastructure of spinal cord neuronal mitochondria was observed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Iron deposition in the injured spinal cord segment was observed by Prussian blue staining. The activity of mitochondrial respiratory complex I in spinal cord tissue was measured by colorimetric assay. Western blot was used to detect the relative protein expression levels of ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1), ferritin light chain (FTL), voltage-dependent anion channel 2 (VDAC2), mitochondrial ferritin (FTMT), CDGSH iron-sulfur domain-containing protein 1 (CISD1), and CDGSH iron-sulfur domain-containing protein 2 (CISD2) in mitochondria.
Compared with the sham operation group, the model group exhibited significantly increased bladder maximum capacity and bladder compliance (P<0.01), and decreased leak point pressure (P<0.01). Histologically, the spinal cord tissue displayed extensive vacuolization, severe erythrocyte infiltration, and significant iron deposition. TEM revealed swollen mitochondria with vanished cristae and partial membrane rupture. Moreover, the activity of mitochondrial respiratory complex I was significantly reduced (P<0.01). Protein expressions of FTH1 and FTL, as well as mitochondrial FTMT, CISD1, and CISD2, were significantly down-regulated (P<0.01), whereas VDAC2 expression was significantly up-regulated (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, the moxibustion group showed decreased bladder maximum capacity and bladder compliance (P<0.05), and increased leak point pressure (P<0.05). The histopathological damage was notably alleviated, with reduced erythrocyte infiltration and iron deposition. Mitochondrial morphology was largely intact, with an increased number of normal mitochondria. The activity of mitochondrial respiratory complex I was significantly elevated (P<0.05). Furthermore, the protein expressions of FTH1, FTL, FTMT, CISD1, and CISD2 were significantly up-regulated (P<0.05, P<0.01), while VDAC2 was significantly down-regulated (P<0.05).
Moxibustion at CV4 can improve bladder function in rats with urinary retention after SCI. The mechanism may be related to its function in regulating mitochondrial iron metabolism in spinal cord tissue, thereby repairing the injured spinal cord and promoting the micturition reflex.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on mitochondrial unfolded protein response-associated proteins in the colon tissue of mice with functional constipation].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Wang W, Li Y, Zeng W, Yan X, He Z, Xiao X et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) at "Tianshu" (ST25) and "Shangjuxu" (ST37) acupoints on the expressions of mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) - related proteins in the colon tissue of functional constipation (FC) model mice, so as to explore its potential mechanisms underlying improvement of FC.
Eighteen male C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into 3 groups:normal control (NC), FC model (M), and EA (n=6 per group). The FC model was established by gavage of loperamide suspension (1 mg/mL, 0.1 mL/10 g), twice daily for 14 d. The EA group received alternating unilateral EA stimulation of ST25 and ST37(3 Hz/15 Hz, an electric current intensity being able to induce slight tremor of the mouse's limbs) for 20 min, once daily, 5 d a week for 2 weeks. The mice in the NC and M groups underwent equivalent restraint. Gastrointestinal transit function was assessed by measuring the first blue stool discharge time, 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, and intestinal propulsion rate. Histopathological changes of the colon tissue were examined by H.E. staining, and the mitochondrial ultrastructure of colonic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) was observed by using a transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and the mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) levels were assayed using flow cytometry, and the mitochondrial ATP content in the colon tissue was measured using colorimetric assay. The immunohistochemistry stain was employed to detect the expressions of key UPRmt markers heat shock protein-60 (HSP60) and LON protease 1 (LONP1) in the colon tissue.
Compared with the NC group, the M group exhibited a significant increase in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a considerable reduction in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP level, ATP content, and the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). Following EA intervention, compared to the M group, the EA group showed a marked decrease in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a notable increase in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP, ATP content, and the expression of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). The results of ultrastructure showed that the mitochondria of SMCs in the colon tissue was significantly swollen, with membrane damage and severe cristae rupture in the M group, while in the EA group, the mitochondrial swelling was mild, with significant improvement in the membrane and cristae integrity of the SMCs.
EA at ST25 and ST37 can effectively ameliorate gastrointestinal dysfunction and restore mitochondrial integrity in colonic SMCs of FC mice, which may be associated with its functions in up-regulating the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins to activate UPRmt.

papers.title: [Research on the underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture in improving colonic dysmotility in ulcerative colitis mice based on cyclic nucleotide-gated cation channels].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Li S, Huang Q, Huang Q, Wu Q, Yu S
papers.abstract:
To study the mechanism of electroacupuncture (EA) of "Shangjuxu"(ST37) underlying improvement of colonic dysmotility in ulcerative colitis (UC) mice through regulating hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated cation channel 2 (HCN2).
Male C57BL/6J mice were randomized into control, model and EA groups, with 8 mice in each group. The UC model was established by giving 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) to the mice. EA (2 Hz/100 Hz, 0.9 mA) was applied at bilateral ST37 for 20 min, once a day for 7 d. The body weight, stool appearance and bloody stool conditions were recorded and the disease activity index (DAI) score was determined. The morphological changes of the colonic tissue were observed after H.E. staining. The changes of colonic motility before and after EA intervention were assessed by using in vivo and in vitro electrophysiological methods. The colonic transit time (glass bead method) and intestinal propulsion rate (ink mark method) were calculated. The positive expression of colonic HCN2, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (TPH1), and serotonin transporter (SERT) were detected by immunofluorescence staining. The expression levels of TPH1 and SERT mRNAs and proteins were detected using real-time quantitative PCR and Western blot separately. The Vil1MerCreMerHCN2fl/fl mice were randomly divided into a control group and an induction group, with 8 mice in each group. The Vil1MerCreMerHCN2fl/fl mice were specifically conditionally knocked out the HCN2 gene in the intestinal epithelium. The mice in the induction group were injected with 5 mg/mL tamoxifen. ELISA was used to detect the contents of 5-HT and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) in the serum. The RIN-14B cells were divided into a normal group and a transfection group. The transfection group was knocked down the expression of HCN2 in the RIN-14B cells. ELISA was used to detect the contents of 5-HT and cAMP in the cell supernatants. Real-time quantitative PCR was used to detect the mRNA expressions of HCN2 and TPH1 in the RIN-14B cells.
In contrast to the control group, the model group showed a significant decrease in the body weight and a notable increase in the DAI score and histopathological score (all P<0.001). In vivo and in vitro electrophysiology showed that DSS mice had significant colonic motility dysfunction, decreased frequency, amplitude, and the area under the curve (AUC) of colonic pressure curves (all P<0.001). Colonic transit time was strikingly prolonged while propulsion rate was significantly lower in DSS mice (all P<0.001). Expression of colonic HCN2, co-localized with 5-HT, were markedly increased (P<0.001), along with elevated expression of 5-HT, TPH1 and SERT (all P<0.001). All the increase and decrease of the indexes mentioned above were reversed by EA ( P<0.001, P<0.01, P<0.05). Conditional deletion of HCN2 in the intestinal epithelium markedly reduced the serum contents of 5-HT and cAMP ( P<0.001). Knockdown of HCN2 in RIN-14B cells reduced the expression levels of HCN2and TPH1 mRNAs (P<0.001), along with a significant decrease of the contents of 5-HT and cAMP in the cell supernatant (P<0.001).
EA at ST37 can improve colonic dysmotility in UC mice by modulating the expression of HCN2 in enterochromaffin cells and regulating the release of 5-HT.

papers.title: [Effects of electroacupuncture on apoptosis and inflammation in rats with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease based on integrated stress responses].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Huang L, Duan L, Chen L, Xue T, Yang S, He Q et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of electroacupuncture on rats with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), so as to explore its potential mechanisms.
Thirty SD rats were randomly divided into a control group, a model group, and an electroacupuncture group, with 10 rats in each group. The COPD model was established by combining lipopolysaccharide instillation with smoke exposure. Following successful modeling, the electroacupuncture group received bilateral electroacupuncture at the "Feishu"(BL23) and "Zusanli"(ST36) points (dense-disperse wave, 4 Hz/20 Hz, 1-3 mA), once daily, 20 min/session, for 2 consecutive weeks. General conditions of rats in each group were compared before and after intervention. Post-intervention, histopathological changes in lung tissue were observed via HE staining. Serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and IL-1β were measured by ELISA. TUNEL staining was used to detect apoptosis in lung tissue, and the apoptosis index was calculated. The protein and mRNA expressions of protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase (PERK), eukaryotic initiation factor 2α (eIF2α), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), B-cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2), and Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax) in lung tissue were detected by Western blot and real-time quantative PCR respectively.
Compared with the control group, rats in the model group exhibited poorer general condition after intervention, with significant pathological damage in lung tissue;serum IL-6, TNF-α and IL-1β levels and the apoptosis index in lung tissue were significantly increased (P<0.01), and serum IL-10 level was decreased (P<0.01). The protein and mRNA expressions of PERK, eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP and Bax in lung tissue were increased (P<0.01, P<0.05), while Bcl-2 protein and mRNA expressions were decreased (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, rats in the electroacupuncture group showed improved general condition and reduced pathological damage in lung tissue;serum IL-6, TNF-α and IL-1β levels and apoptosis index were decreased (P<0.05, P<0.01), and serum IL-10 level was increased (P<0.01). The protein and mRNA expressions of PERK, eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP and Bax in lung tissue were decreased (P<0.05), and Bcl-2 protein and mRNA expressions were increased (P<0.05).
Electroacupuncture ameliorates lung injury in COPD rats, potentially by inhibiting the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP cascade of the integrated stress response pathway, thereby reducing apoptosis and inflammation.

papers.title: [Mechanism of electroacupuncture at "Yingxiang-Hegu" (LI20-LI4) acupoints ameliorating allergic rhinitis in rats via modulating ILC2s through the IL-33/ST2 pathway].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Wu H, Lü H, Zhang H, Hu Z, Li L, Zhai C et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the regulatory effects of electroacupuncture at "Yingxiang-Hegu" (LI20-LI4) acupoints on the interleukin (IL)-33/growth stimulation expressed gene 2 (ST2) signaling pathway and type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) in the nasal mucosa of allergic rhinitis (AR) rats, and to explore its therapeutic mechanism for AR.
Forty-eight SD rats were randomly divided into a control group (n=12) and a modeling group (n=36). Ovalbumin (OVA)-induced AR model was established. Thirty-six successfully modeled rats were further randomized into a model group (n=12), a western medicine group (n=12), and an electroacupuncture group (n=12). The electroacupuncture group received acupuncture at the paired points "Yingxiang-Hegu"(LI20-LI4) with the ipsilateral LI20 and LI4 points connected to an electroacupuncture device. Stimulation parameters were set as follows:sparse-dense wave, frequency 2 Hz /100 Hz, current intensity 1-2 mA, needle retention for 20 min. The western medicine group received oral administration of loratadine(0.1 mg/100 g). Interventions were administered once daily for 14 consecutive days in all groups. Nasal allergy symptoms (nose scratching, sneezing and nasal discharge) were observed and scored before and after modeling, as well as after intervention. After intervention, histopathological change in the nasal mucosal tissue was examined via hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining. ELISA was used to detect serum ovalbumin-specific immunoglobulin E (OVA-sIgE), IL-9, and IL-13 levels. Immunofluorescence double staining was used to assess ST2 and thymic cell antigen 1 (Thy1, also known as CD90) positive expression and ILC2s numbers in nasal mucosal tissue. Real-time quantitative PCR was used to detect the mRNA expression levels of GATA binding protein 3(GATA3), retinoic acid-related orphan receptor alpha (ROR-α), IL-33, ST2, IL-1 receptor accessory protein (IL-1RAcP), myeloid differentiation primary-response protein 88 (MyD88), i IL-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4), and nuclear factor κB p65 subunit (NF-κB p65) in nasal mucosal tissue. Western blot was used to measure the protein expression levels of IL-33, ST2 and MyD88 in nasal mucosal tissue.
Following OVA sensitization, nasal allergy symptom scores in the model group were significantly elevated compared to the control group (all>5 points, P<0.001), indicating successful modeling. After intervention, the nasal allergy symptom scores in the model group remained persistently high compared to the control group (P<0.001). HE staining revealed disrupted nasal mucosal barrier and marked inflammatory response. Serum OVA-sIgE, IL-9 and IL-13 levels were significantly elevated (P<0.001);the number of ILC2s in the nasal mucosa significantly increased (P<0.001), with enhanced fluorescence intensities of ST2 and Thy1 (P<0.001). GATA3, ROR-α, IL-33, ST2, IL-1RAcP, MyD88, IRAK4 and NF-κB p65 mRNA expression levels were elevated (P<0.001, P<0.01), while IL-33, ST2 and MyD88 protein expression levels were increased (P<0.001). Compared with the model group, both the electroacupuncture and western medicine groups showed a reversal of all the above indicators (P<0.001, P<0.01, P<0.05);HE staining revealed reduced inflammatory infiltration in the nasal mucosa and improved tissue structural integrity. No statistically significant differences were observed between the electroacupuncture group and the western medicine group for any of the measured indicators.
Electroacupuncture at "Yingxiang-Hegu"(LI20-LI4) acupoints ameliorates OVA-induced nasal mucosal inflammatory changes in AR rats. This effect may be mediated by inhibiting the IL-33/ST2 signaling pathway and down-regulating ILC2s expression, thereby improving allergic rhinitis in rats.

summary.results: 전침은 모델군에 비해 비강 점막 염증과 OVA-sIgE, IL-9, IL-13, ILC2 및 IL-33/ST2 관련 발현을 유의하게 낮췄고, 로라타딘군과 유사한 결과를 보였다.

papers.title: [Mechanism of acupotomy in regulating oxidative stress injury of cartilage in rabbits with knee osteoarthritis via the Sirt1/Nrf2/NQO1 signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Wang M, Zhang Z, Cao Y, Li K, Zhang Z, An K et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of acupotomy on the sirtuin 1 (Sirt1)/ nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/ NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1(NQO1) signaling pathway of oxidative stress in the cartilage tissue of rabbits with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), so as to explore its underlying mechanism in ameliorating cartilage injury.
Twenty-four male New Zealand rabbits were randomly divided into normal control, model, acupotomy, and acupotomy+inhibitor (EX-527, an inhibitor of Sirt1) groups, with 6 rabbits in each group. The KOA model was established by using the modified Videman method. After successful modeling, the acupotomy group received acupotomy releasing at the medial collateral ligament, lateral collateral ligament, medial patellar retinaculum, lateral patellar retinaculum, patellar ligament, and cord-like nodular points of the left lower limb, once weekly for 4 weeks. The acupotomy + inhibitor group received intraperitoneal injection of the Sirt1 inhibitor EX-527 30 min before every session of acupotomy intervention, once weekly for 4 weeks. Before intervention and one week after the final intervention, the Lequesne MG disability index score (Lequesne MG score) assessment and passive range of motion (PROM) measurement were performed. The cartilage tissue was collected for observing histopathological changes after H.E. and Safranin O-Fast Green staining, detecting the level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) with immunofluorescence stain, detecting the activity of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) with colorimetric assay and enzymatic reaction combined with DTNB colorimetric method respectively, and for measuring the contents of total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC) with ABTS method, and MDA with TBA method. The contents of IL-1β and TNF-α in the synovial fluid were measured using ELISA. The expression levels of Sirt1, Nrf2, NQO1, recombinant A disintegrin and metalloproteinase with thrombospondin 5 (ADAMTS5) and matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) proteins, and Sirt1, Nrf2 and NQO1 mRNAs in the cartilage tissue were detected using Western blot and real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR, separately.
Compared with the normal control group, the model group showed a significant increase in the Lequesne MG score, contents of IL-1β, TNF-α and MDA, immunofluorescence intensity of ROS, and expression levels of Nrf2, MMP3 and ADAMTS5 proteins, and Nrf2 mRNA (P<0.01, P<0.05), and a significant decease in the PROM, contents of SOD, GSH-Px and T-AOC, and expression levels of Sirt1 protein and mRNA (P<0.01). In contrast to those of the model group, both the increase and decrease of the indexes mentioned above in the acupotomy group were all reversed (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, the Lequesne MG score, contents of TNF-α, MDA, and immunofluorescence intensity of ROS were obviously decreased (P<0.01, P<0.05), while the PROM, expression levels of Nrf2, Sirt1 and NQO1 mRNAs strikingly increased in the acupotomy+inhibitor group (P<0.01). The effects of acupotomy were significantly superior to those of acupotomy+inhibitor in lowering the Lequesne score, contents of TNF-α, IL-1β, MDA, ROS immunofluorescence intensity, expression levels of MMP3 and ADAMTS-5 proteins (P<0.01, P<0.05), and in increasing the PROM, contents of SOD, GSH-Px and T-AOC, expressions of Sirt1, Nrf2 and NQO1 proteins and mRNAs (P<0.01, P<0.05), suggesting a strikingly weakened efficacy of acupotomy after administration of inhibitor EX-527 and an involvement of Sirt1 in acupotomy effect. Morphological observation revealed that in the model group, the cartilage surface of the knee joint became thinner, and the number of chondrocytes was decreased, with disordered arrangement, and Safranin and Fast Green staining showed that the protein polysaccharides were lost. Compared with the model group, the number of chondrocytes was increased, with regular arrangement, clear nuclear and cytoplasmic structures, and the protein polysaccharides was increased in the acupotomy group;but in the acupotomy+inhibitor group, the damage of the cartilage surface was more severe compared to the acupotomy group.
Acupotomy therapy can ameliorate joint function and cartilage pathological damage in KOA rabbits, which may be related to its functions in mitigating oxidative stress and inflammatory responses by activating the Sirt1/Nrf2/NQO1 signaling pathway.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 전임상 결과는 아큐토미의 잠재적 기전을 시사하지만, 사람 KOA에 대한 임상적 유효성과 안전성은 추가 연구가 필요하다.

papers.title: [Electroacupuncture inhibits astrocyte activation and alleviates neuroinflammation in rats with ischemic stroke based on JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Hua W, Zhou Z, Li S, Lan W, Jiang Y, Qiao F et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) intervention on neuroinflammatory response in rats with ischemic stroke by modulating astrocyte activation, based on the Janus kinase 2(JAK2)/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3) signaling pathway.
Forty-five male SD rats were randomly selected as the sham operation group. The ischemic stroke model was established by occlusion of the middle cerebral artery by referring to the modified Zea Longa's suture-occlusion method. Ninety successfully modeled rats were randomly assigned to model group and EA group which were further divided into subgroups based on the intervention time points (1, 3 and 7 d). For rats of the EA group, EA (2 Hz/10 Hz, 1.5 mA) was applied to "Baihui" (GV20) and "Dazhui" (GV14) for 20 min (starting from 2 h post-modeling), once daily for 1, 3 or 7 d. The modified neurological severity score (mNSS) was used to assess neurological deficits, and 2, 3, 5-Triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining was employed to measure the cerebral infarction volume. Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining was used to observe histopathological changes in the ischemic cortex. The protein expression levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), JAK2, STAT3, phosphorylated-JAK2 (p-JAK2), p-STAT3, complement component 3 (C3), and S100 calcium-binding protein A10 (S100A10) in the ischemic brain tissue were detected using Western blot. The contents of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and IL-6 in the ischemic brain tissue were determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The mRNA expression levels of GFAP, JAK2, and STAT3 in the ischemic brain tissue were detected by using quantitative real-time PCR. The double-staining immunofluorescence intensity of GFAP and STAT3 of the ischemic brain tissue was determined using immunofluorescence staining.
Compared with the sham operation group, the model group showed a significant increase in cerebral infarction volume (P<0.01), and mNSS, protein expression levels of GFAP, JAK2, STAT3, p-JAK2, p-STAT3, and C3, contents of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and mRNA expression levels of GFAP, JAK2 and STAT3 at the 1st, 3rd and 7th day (P<0.01), and the immunofluorescence intensity of GFAP and STAT3 co-staining (P<0.01), and a significant reduction in the expression of S100A10 at the 1st, 3rd and 7th day (P<0.01). The ischemic cortex exhibited severe neuronal structural damage, characterized by obvious nuclear pyknosis, cellular swelling and rupture, disordered axonal arrangement and vacuolar changes. After EA intervention, all the increased and decreased levels of the indexes mentioned above were reversed (P<0.05, P<0.01), including obvious improvement of morphology of neurons in the ischemic cortex, characterized by more regular cell arrangement and clearer cellular nucleus. Compared with the group receiving EA for 1 d, the group with 7 d of EA treatment exhibited lower protein expression levels of GFAP, C3 and S100A10 as well as decreased contents of TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6 (P<0.01), while the group receiving EA for 3 d showed up-regulated S100A10 protein expression (P<0.05).
EA can improve neurological deficits and reduce cerebral ischemic volume in ischemic stroke rats, which may be related to its functions in inhibiting the activation of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, mitigating neuroinflammation response mediated by excessive astrocyte activation, and the effects are time-dependent.

papers.title: [Mechanism of acupuncture improving thrombolysis safety in ischemic stroke based on necroptosis mediated by RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Song Y, Li S, Zhao Y, Huang Z, Chang S, Dong H et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of acupuncture on inhibiting necroptosis mediated by the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling pathway in rat model of ischemic stroke, so as to reveal the mechanism underlying the improvement of ultra-time-window thrombolysis safety by acupuncture.
Ninety-nine male successful modeling SD rats were randomly divided into the model, 6 h thrombolysis, and acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis groups, with 33 rats in each group. In addition, 33 SD rats were randomly selected as the sham-operation group. Except for the sham-operation group, rats in the other groups were subjected to the autologous thromboembolism method to establish the ischemic stroke model. Rats in the 6 h thrombolysis group were treated with intravenous thrombolysis using recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) at 6 h after the successful modeling. Rats in the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group were additionally treated with acupuncture at bilateral "Neiguan" (PC6) and "Shuigou" (GV26) for 20 min after the thrombolysis. Neurological function was evaluated by Bederson score. The cerebral infarction volume was measured by 2, 3, 5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was detected by Evans blue permeability assay. Brain water content was measured by the volume specific gravity method. Hemoglobin concentration was detected by spectrophotometry. The protein expressions of RIPK1, RIPK3, and p-MLKL were detected by Western blot. The mRNA expressions of RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL were detected by real-time PCR. The co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells was detected by double immunofluorescence staining.
After modeling, the cerebral blood flow of rats significantly decreased, and the neurobehavioral scores increased (P<0.01). At 24 h after successful modeling, compared with the sham-operation group, the model group had a significant increase in neurobehavioral scores, percentage of infarct volume, and BBB permeability (P<0.01), as well as an elevation in the protein expression level of RIPK1 (P<0.05) , the mRNA expression levels of RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL in the ischemic penumbra (IP, P<0.01, P<0.05), and increased percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP(P<0.01). Following intervention and compared with the model group, the 6 h thrombolysis group had a further increase in BBB permeability, brain water content, and cerebral hemoglobin concentration (P<0.01, P<0.05);elevated protein expression levels of RIPK3 and p-MLKL in the IP (P<0.05);increased mRNA expression levels of RIPK3 and MLKL in the IP (P<0.05);and an increased percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group showed decreased neurobehavioral scores, percentage of infarct volume, BBB permeability, and brain water content (P<0.01, P<0.05);decreased protein and mRNA expression levels of RIPK1 in the IP (P<0.05);and a reduced percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP (P<0.05). Compared with the 6 h thrombolysis group, the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group demonstrated a significant decrease in all the aforementioned indicators (P<0.01, P<0.05).
Timely intervention with acupuncture can improve neurological function, reduce cerebral infarct volume, lower BBB permeability, and decrease the incidence of thrombolytic complications in rats with ischemic stroke after thrombolysis, thereby improving the safety of thrombolysis. Its mechanism may be related to the inhibition of endothelial cell necroptosis mediated by the RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL signaling pathway.
papers.title_ko: 허혈성 뇌졸중에서 아쿠포인트 자침이 RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL 신호경로 매개 괴사성 세포사멸을 억제해 혈전용해 안전성을 높이는 기전

papers.title: [Effects of acupoint catgut embedding regulating AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway on intestinal microbiota and inflammatory response in simple obese rats].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Li Y, Ruan C, Wang W, Li P, Liang F
papers.abstract:
To explore the effects of acupoint catgut embedding on intestinal microbiota and inflammatory response in simple obese rats and its underlying mechanism.
SD rats were fed with high-fat diet to establish simple obesity models, and the model rats were randomly divided into model group, orlistat group, catgut embedding group, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activator (AICAR) group, and catgut embedding + AMPK inhibitor (Compound C) group, with 8 rats in each group. Another 8 SD rats were set as the control group. In the catgut embedding group, catgut embedding was performed at acupoints "Zhongwan" (CV12), "Guanyuan" (CV4), "Zusanli" (ST36), and "Fenglong" (ST40), once a week for 4 consecutive weeks. Rats in the orlistat group received intragastric administration of orlistat at 0.048 g/kg once daily for 4 weeks. Rats in the AICAR group were given tail-vein injection of AICAR at 50 mg/kg once daily for 4 weeks. Rats in the catgut embedding + Compound C group received catgut embedding combined with tail-vein injection of Compound C at 250 μg/kg. Body weight and body length were measured and Lee's index was calculated. Fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and fasting insulin (FINS) were detected and the insulin resistance index was calculated. Serum levels of total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C) were determined by biochemical analyzer. Serum contents of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and interleukin-10 (IL-10) were measured by ELISA. Pathological changes of colon tissues were observed by HE staining. Immunofluorescence was used to detect the positive expression of Occludin and Claudin-1 in colon tissue. The abundance of intestinal bacterial genera was determined by PCR. Western blot was applied to detect the protein expression of AMPK/sirtuin-1 (SIRT1)/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1α (PGC-1α) pathway in colon and adipose tissues.
Compared with the control group, the model group showed significantly increased body weight, Lee's index, serum TC, TG, LDL-C, TNF-α, IL-6, LPS, FPG, FINS, insulin resistance index, as well as the abundances of Enterococcus and Desulfovibrio (P<0.05);while serum IL-10 and HDL-C levels, the abundances of Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, and Akkermansia, the fluorescence intensity of Occludin and Claudin-1 in colon tissues, the p-AMPK/AMPK ratio, and the protein levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α in colon and adipose tissues were decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the model group, the orlistat group, catgut embedding group and AICAR group exhibited significantly decreased body weight, Lee's index, serum TC, TG, LDL-C, TNF-α, IL-6, LPS, FPG, FINS, insulin resistance index, and the abundances of Enterococcus and Desulfovibrio (P<0.05);whereas serum IL-10 and HDL-C levels, the abundances of Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Akkermansia, the fluorescence intensity of Occludin and Claudin-1 in colon tissues, the p-AMPK/AMPK ratio, and the protein levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α in colon and adipose tissues were elevated (P<0.05). Compared with the catgut embedding group, the catgut embedding + Compound C group had significantly higher body weight, Lee's index, serum TC, TG, LDL-C, TNF-α, IL-6, LPS, FPG, FINS, insulin resistance index, and abundances of Enterococcus and Desulfovibrio (P<0.05);while serum IL-10 and HDL-C levels, the abundances of Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Akkermansia, colon Occludin and Claudin-1 fluorescence intensity, p-AMPK/AMPK ratio, and SIRT1 and PGC-1α protein expression in colon and adipose tissues were reduced (P<0.05).
Acupoint catgut embedding can alleviate systemic low-grade inflammatory response, regulate blood lipid metabolism, modulate the abundance of beneficial intestinal bacteria, and repair intestinal barrier function in simple obese rats. Its mechanism may be related to the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling pathway.

papers.title: [Research progress on brain-body interaction mechanisms of acupuncture in treating primary dysmenorrhea].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Zeng Y, Chen X, Yu Z, Yu S, Yang S
papers.abstract: Primary dysmenorrhea (PD) is a common gynecological disorder affecting women of reproductive age worldwide, characterized by high prevalence, recurrent attacks and impaired quality of life. Acupuncture has definite therapeutic effects on PD, and related studies on its mechanism are increasingly deepening. The core pathogenesis of PD is the disordered brain-body bidirectional interaction. From the perspective of brain-body interaction, this paper systematically summarizes the mechanisms of acupuncture in treating PD, including synchronously regulating central networks such as default mode network, sensorimotor network, and descending pain modulatory system, modulating hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and modulating signaling pathways including Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor-κB, and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin, as well as improving uterine local pathological status, optimizing uterine blood flow, correcting prostaglandin imbalance, and relieving smooth muscle spasm. These effects synergistically block the brain-body vicious cycle of PD and achieve multi-system, multi-level holistic regulation and long-lasting analgesia.

papers.title: [Temperature-dependent effects of thermal stimulation at "Zusanli" (ST36) on visceral hyperalgesia and SRD neuronal electrical activity in rats with acute colonic mucosal injury].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Li Y, Zhang Z, Sun X, Wang X, Deng L, Zheng H et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect and dose-response relationship of thermal stimulation at "Zusanli" (ST36) with different temperatures on alleviating visceral hyperalgesia in rats with acute colonic mucosal injury, so as to explore its underlying mechanism focusing on the electrical activity of the subnucleus reticularis dorsalis (SRD) in the medulla.
(1) Eighteen SD rats were randomly divided into normal and model groups, with 9 rats in each group. The acute colonic mucosal injury model was established by mustard oil enema. The structural and pathological changes of colonic tissue were observed by colonoscopy and HE staining. The expressions of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) in rat colonic tissue were detected by immunofluorescence staining. (2) Thirty SD rats were randomly divided into normal group, model group, 44 ℃, 48 ℃, and 52 ℃ thermal stimulation groups (n=6 in each group). After modeling, thermal stimulation with the corresponding temperature was applied to "Zusanli" (ST36) in each stimulation group. Visceral pain was induced by colorectal distension. The area under the curve (AUC) of rectus abdominis electromyogram (EMG) was evaluated by EMG recording, and the inhibition rate of noxious EMG by thermal stimulation at different temperatures was calculated. (3) Pseudorabies virus (PRV) retrograde tracing was employed in 3 normal rats to label SRD neurons receiving dual projections from both ST36 and the colon. (4) Twenty-four model rats were randomly divided into 44 ℃, 48 ℃, and 52 ℃ thermal stimulation groups, with 8 rats in each group. Multi-channel in vivo electrophysiological technique was used to record the electrical activity of SRD neurons. The changes in SRD neuronal firing within 1 h of acute mustard oil perfusion and the inhibitory effect of thermal stimulation at different temperatures on their firing were observed.
After modeling and compared with the normal group, the rats' colonic mucosa showed congestion, edema, structural destruction, and obvious inflammatory cell infiltration, with significantly increased distribution of CGRP and TRPV1 positive nerve fibers (P<0.05) and a significantly increased AUC of rectus abdominis EMG (P<0.001). Compared with the model group, After 48 ℃ and 52 ℃ thermal stimulation, the evoked rectus abdominis EMG was significantly reduced (P<0.001);while there was no statistically significant difference in AUC after 44℃ thermal stimulation. The inhibition rates at 48 ℃ and 52 ℃ were significantly higher than that at 44℃ (P<0.05), with no significant difference between 48 ℃ and 52 ℃. Morphologically, PRV retrograde tracing revealed neurons in the medullary SRD region that were single-labeled from the colon or ST36, as well as double-labeled neurons. Electrophysiologically, the firing frequency of SRD neurons increased rapidly at 5 min after mustard oil instillation, and the increase persisted for 30 min (P<0.05). During this high-firing period, thermal stimulation at 48 ℃ and 52 ℃ significantly suppressed the firing frequency (P<0.01, P<0.05), whereas 44 ℃ stimulation had no such effect.
Noxious thermal stimulation at 48 ℃ and 52 ℃ can effectively alleviate visceral hyperalgesia in rats with acute colonic mucosal injury, which may be related to inhibiting nociceptive discharge of medullary SRD neurons. Considering both central inhibitory effect and local skin safety, 48 ℃ appears to be the optimal intervention temperature.

papers.title: Ginkgolide B drives cardiomyocyte proliferation and myocardial regeneration through TLR4/NF-κB/HIF-1α-regulated glycolytic reprogramming.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.authors: Zhang H, Tang K, Cai Y, Feng Z, Yang Y, Qian L et al.
papers.abstract:
Myocardial infarction (MI) continues to contribute substantially to global mortality and is characterized by irreversible cardiomyocyte loss and limited regenerative capacity in the adult heart. Ginkgolide B (GB), a bioactive compound used in traditional Chinese medicine, has well-documented cardioprotective effects; however, whether it promotes cardiomyocyte proliferation and myocardial regeneration, and through which mechanisms, remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential and underlying molecular mechanisms of GB in promoting cardiomyocyte proliferation and cardiac regeneration.
The therapeutic effects of GB were assessed in cardiomyocyte (CM) cell lines and mouse models of apical resection (AR) and MI. To define the underlying mechanism, we combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, RNA sequencing, and targeted metabolite profiling. The interaction between GB and TLR4 was evaluated using a cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). The dependency on the TLR4/NF-κB/HIF-1α pathway and glycolysis were pharmacologically validated using 2-deoxy-d-glucose (2-DG, glycolysis inhibitor) and Bay 11-7082 (NF-κB inhibitor).
GB enhanced CM proliferation and angiogenesis in vitro, and improved cardiac function, reduced infarct size, and promoted CM proliferation in neonatal and adult mouse models. Mechanistically, GB interacted directly with TLR4, activated the NF-κB/HIF-1α signaling axis, and promoted a shift toward glycolytic metabolism. Inhibition of NF-κB or glycolysis abolished GB-induced CM proliferation, glycolytic activity, and myocardial regeneration.
GB promotes cardiomyocyte proliferation and cardiac regeneration through TLR4/NF-κB/HIF-1α-dependent regulation of glycolytic metabolism. These findings support the potential of GB as a plant-derived therapeutic candidate for ischemic heart disease.

papers.title: Zuojin Wan reverses cetuximab resistance in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer via the NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ axes.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.authors: Liu X, Chen Y, Jiang Y, Sui H, Liang T, Meng J et al.
papers.abstract:
Cetuximab (CET), a monoclonal antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), serves as a cornerstone therapeutic option for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). However, patients with KRAS-mutant CRC present inherent resistance to CET, which directly compromises its clinical efficacy and therapeutic benefits. Zuojin Wan (ZJW), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting of Coptis chinensis Franch. and Evodia rutaecarpa (Juss.) Benth., has been documented to exert potent antitumor activity; nevertheless, its potential role in reversing CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined.
This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of ZJW in overcoming CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and further characterize its key molecular targets and regulatory mechanisms.
In vitro experiments were conducted using two KRAS-mutated CRC cell lines, HCT116 and SW620. The synergistic antiproliferative effect of ZJW combined with CET was assessed via CCK-8 assay and colony formation assay. Ferroptosis induction mediated by the combination treatment was verified by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) depletion, ferrous ion (Fe2+) accumulation, and observing characteristic mitochondrial morphological alterations using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were detected to evaluate intracellular oxidative stress. Transcriptome sequencing, Western blot analysis and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were performed to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms, while plasmid transfection and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were carried out for functional validation. A nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model was established to evaluate the antitumor efficacy of the combined treatment in vivo, and immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was performed to detect the expression of relevant proteins. The primary bioactive components of ZJW were identified by mass spectrometry, and network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict the potential interactions between these active components and CRC-related signaling pathways.
ZJW synergistically augmented the CET-mediated suppression of KRAS-mutated CRC cell proliferation and triggered significant ferroptosis, as evidenced by elevated lipid peroxidation, reduced GSH levels, increased Fe2+ accumulation, shrunken mitochondria with condensed cristae, and markedly enhanced intracellular oxidative stress. Combination treatment with ZJW and CET significantly downregulated the expression of core proteins involved in the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes, thereby disrupting intracellular redox homeostasis. Silencing of NRF2 or DHODH facilitated ferroptosis and sensitized CRC cells to CET, whereas overexpression of these two molecules abolished the synergistic antitumor effect of ZJW plus CET. In the nude mouse xenograft model, the combined regimen notably suppressed tumor growth and decreased tumor weight, and modulated the expression of ferroptosis-associated markers (NRF2, DHODH) and the lipid peroxidation indicator 4-HNE in tumor tissues. Mass spectrometry identified the major bioactive constituents of ZJW, and network pharmacology analysis predicted their potential involvement in multiple CRC-related pathways, including antioxidant defense and ferroptosis regulation.
ZJW reverses CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC by inhibiting the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes to induce ferroptosis. This study provides a solid scientific basis for the clinical translation of ZJW as an adjuvant therapeutic strategy to boost the efficacy of CET in CRC treatment.

papers.title: Therapeutic efficacy and dosing regimen evidence synthesis of Ursolic Acid for liver injury: A preclinical systematic review with machine learning.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.authors: Peng XY, Miao J, Du W, Shi L, Li W, Lu XR et al.
papers.abstract:
Ursolic acid (UA), a pentacyclic triterpene, shows hepatoprotective efficacy and favorable safety in various animal models of liver injury. However, robust preclinical evidence remains scarce.
To synthesize the preclinical evidence for UA and explore how UA dose and treatment duration are associated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) improvement in animal models of liver injury.
This preclinical systematic review integrating meta-analysis and machine learning followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA).
Relevant preclinical studies through April 11, 2026 were systematically retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, OVID, CNKI and Wanfang. Machine learning analyses were used to identify factors associated with ALT improvement, particularly human equivalent dose (HED) and treatment duration.
Forty-seven articles were included in this analysis. UA markedly improved histopathological parameters, liver function, biochemical parameters, serum lipid levels, oxidative stress indicators, and inflammatory markers in liver injury animal models. Random forest was selected as the final predictive model. The analysis further identified model administration route, treatment duration, HED, and time of administration as key determinants for the improvement rate of ALT. An exploratory HED range of approximately 5-7 mg/kg was associated with greater predicted ALT improvement.
The study indicates that UA exerts hepatoprotective effects in animal models of liver injury. Potential mechanisms include modulation of the gut-liver axis, attenuation of hepatic and systemic oxidative stress, and suppression of inflammation and fibrosis. Given the exploratory nature of these preclinical findings, the translational potential of UA warrants further rigorous validation.

papers.title: Comparative effectiveness of Neiguan acupoint stimulation in preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting following general anesthesia: A network meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Li Y, Mao L, Zhao C, Liu M, Yu J, Yang X et al.
papers.abstract:
To compare the relative efficacy of different Neiguan (PC6) acupoint stimulation modalities, alone or combined with antiemetics, for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV).
Eleven English and Chinese databases were searched for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) up to March 2026. Primary outcomes were the incidence of PONV, postoperative nausea (PON), and postoperative vomiting (POV). The secondary outcome was the number of patients requiring antiemetic rescue. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool and CINeMA. Frequentist pairwise and network meta-analyses were conducted using Stata 17.0 and R 4.4.1, and interventions were ranked by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).
Sixty-three RCTs involving 7,874 participants and 14 interventions were included. All PC6 stimulation modalities (acupuncture, electroacupuncture, acupressure, or transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation [TEAS]) reduced PONV, PON, and POV. No significant differences were observed between any stimulation modality and a single antiemetic. Among the stimulation modalities, electroacupuncture ranked highest overall, followed by TEAS and acupuncture, whereas acupressure ranked lowest. When combined with antiemetics, TEAS plus two antiemetics was most effective for PONV and POV (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.33-0.76; RR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.27-0.68; SUCRA = 99%, 93%). For PON and the need for antiemetic rescue, acupuncture plus two antiemetics appeared to be the most effective (RR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.06-0.77; RR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.12-0.81; SUCRA = 95%, 92%). However, this result was based on a single study. After excluding this comparison in sensitivity analyses, TEAS plus two antiemetics remained the most effective intervention.
Electroacupuncture ranked as the most effective PC6 stimulation modality. The combination of PC6 stimulation and antiemetics was more effective than antiemetics alone, with TEAS plus two antiemetics showing the best overall performance. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, highlighting the need for further high-quality studies.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture for Pain Relief During Ultrasonic Periodontal Scaling in Patients with Moderate to Severe Periodontitis: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Ng X, Zheng Y, Liu K, Wang Y, Wang J, Chen Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Ultrasonic periodontal scaling is an essential component of nonsurgical periodontal therapy but is frequently accompanied by substantial pain in patients with moderate to severe periodontitis. Procedural pain and associated anxiety may negatively affect patient tolerance, treatment compliance, and overall clinical outcomes. However, effective and safe nonpharmacological approaches for alleviating pain during periodontal scaling remain limited.
To evaluate the analgesic efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture (EA) during ultrasonic scaling in patients with moderate to severe periodontitis.
This single-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial enrolled 98 participants with moderate to severe periodontitis scheduled for ultrasonic periodontal scaling. Participants were randomly assigned to the EA group (n = 49) or the sham electroacupuncture (SA) group (n = 49). Both groups received stimulation at bilateral Hegu (LI4) and Yatongxue during a single treatment session. The primary outcome was intraoperative whole-mouth pain assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included tooth sensitivity measured by VAS, Modified Dental Anxiety Scale (MDAS) and changes in vital signs, including blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation. Between-group differences in VAS outcomes were analyzed using nonparametric tests, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was applied to adjust baseline differences. Subgroup analyses were conducted using a general linear model.
Compared with SA, EA significantly reduced intraoperative whole-mouth pain, with a Hodges-Lehmann estimated median difference of -1.17 (95% CI: -2.00 to -0.33; Z = -2.66, P = 0.008) and tooth sensitivity was -0.83 (95% CI: -1.67 to -0.17; Z = -2.250, P = 0.024). ANCOVA demonstrated significantly lower postoperative dental anxiety in the EA group after adjusting for baseline MDAS (adjusted mean difference = -1.320, 95% CI: -2.450 to -0.190, P = 0.023). EA was associated with a modest reduction in systolic blood pressure (adjusted mean difference = -5.730, 95% CI: -9.972 to -1.488, P = 0.009), with no significant changes in diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, or oxygen saturation. No serious adverse events were reported.
EA effectively reduces pain during ultrasonic scaling in patients with moderate to severe periodontitis, as well as tooth sensitivity, and dental anxiety without affecting vital sign stability.

papers.title: Valerian, chamomile, and lavender for insomnia and sleep disturbance: a narrative review of mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and safety.
papers.authors: Alhaj OA, Elsahoryi NA, Alfailakawi O, Trabelsi K, Pandi-Perumal SR, Pakpour A et al.
papers.abstract:
Synthesize the botanical, mechanistic, clinical, and safety evidence for valerian (Valeriana officinalis L.), German chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.), and lavender (Lavandula angustifolia Mill.) in adults with insomnia disorder or sleep disturbance and to link their traditional sedative and anxiolytic applications with the current pharmacological evidence.
This study was designed as a narrative review and informed by a structured search of Scopus and PubMed/MEDLINE from inception to 30 June 2026, with results restricted to English-language publications. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical practice guidelines were given priority among the 1655 records (1282 after duplicate removal), and hand searching was conducted. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was conducted; strength of evidence was summarized based on the methodological appraisals reported in the included systematic reviews.
Valerian had minimal and inconsistent effects on subjective sleep quality, no consistent effects on objective sleep latency or total sleep time, and a low methodological quality evidence base. Chamomile decreased Sleep Quality scores in a small and heterogeneous sample of trials, and there were few, small, and inconsistent insomnia-specific trials. Limited evidence suggests that oral lavender oil in the form of standardized lavender oil (Silexan) influences disturbed sleep, which seems to be mediated mainly by reduced anxiety in patients with anxiety. The results are not transferable across products because of differences in preparation, dose, route of application, and study populations.
The evidence did not support any of the three botanicals as an alternative to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia or guideline-based pharmacotherapy. Despite limited evidence, some botanicals are used by patients to address sleep issues and should be discussed with the patient, including benefits, product variability, and safety. Well-powered trials of chemotyped products using objective outcomes in well-defined insomnia populations and powered adverse-event monitoring are needed.

papers.title: Acupuncture may modulates synaptic plasticity in the lateral reins nucleus of CUMS depression rats through GABAB1-CREB-BDNF signaling.
papers.authors: Yao D, Li M, Li J, Zeng J, You Z, Li J et al.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore the therapeutic effects of acupuncture (AP) on depression induced by chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) in rats and its underlying mechanisms through the GABAB1-CREB-BDNF signaling pathway. Male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomly assigned into five groups: Control, CUMS (chronic unpredictable mild stress), CUMS+FXT (fluoxetine treatment), CUMS+AP (acupuncturetreatment), and CUMS+AP+ANT (acupuncture with GABAB receptor antagonist). Depression was induced using the CUMS protocol, and behavioral assessments including the Open Field Test (OFT), Forced Swim Test (FST), Elevated Plus Maze (EPM), and Sucrose Preference Test (SPT) were conducted to evaluate depressive-like behaviors. Golgi staining was employed to measure dendritic length and spine density of lateral habenula neurons, while synaptic ultrastructure was analyzed via transmission electron microscopy. Protein and gene expressions of GABAB1, PKA, CREB, BDNF, CaMKII, and NMDAR in lateral habenula tissue were quantified using Western blot and RT-PCR, respectively. Results indicated that compared to the CUMS group, the CUMS+AP group demonstrated improved sucrose preference, increased open field central residence time, and reduced immobility duration in FST. Transmission electron microscopy revealed enhanced synaptic density and reduced neuronal swelling in the CUMS+AP group. Acupuncture also upregulated the expressions of proteins GABAB1, CREB, and BDNF compared to the CUMS group, while additional levels of PKA, p-CREB, PSD95, and SYP were significantly elevated, though NMDAR expression was downregulated. Notably, the therapeutic effects of AP were inhibited in the CUMS+AP+ANT group, confirming the involvement of the GABAB1-CREB-BDNF pathway. In conclusion, acupuncture alleviates depressive symptoms in CUMS rats by modulating synaptic plasticity and activating the GABAB1-CREB-BDNF signaling pathway, offering a promising neuroprotective mechanism for depression treatment.

papers.title: Effect of Wrist-Ankle Acupuncture for Refractory Postoperative Sore Throat Despite Prophylaxis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Xie C, Yu L, Wang X, Jiang Y, Wang Y, Song J et al.
papers.abstract:
Postoperative sore throat remains a common complication following tracheal intubation, despite prophylaxis with pharmacological and non-pharmacological measures. Wrist-ankle acupuncture, a form of acupuncture, is a known analgesic technique. However, its efficacy for postoperative sore throat remains uncertain.
This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of wrist-ankle acupuncture in alleviating postoperative sore throat that persists despite standard prophylactic measures.
This prospective, patient- and assessor-blinded randomized clinical trial was conducted in China. A total of 120 patients with postoperative sore throat were enrolled and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive wrist-ankle acupuncture or sham acupuncture. Upon developing postoperative sore throat, participants received a single session of either wrist-ankle acupuncture (needle insertion at specific acupoints) or sham acupuncture (blunt-tipped needles at the same locations without breaking the skin). The primary outcome was a numerical rating scale score for sore throat immediately after treatment. Secondary outcomes included numerical rating scale scores at 20min, 1h, 6h, and 24h after acupuncture began and the incidence of hoarseness and dry mouth.
The mean (standard deviation [SD]) of the numerical rating scale score for postoperative sore throat immediately after treatment was significantly lower in the wrist-ankle acupuncture group than in the sham acupuncture group (0.9 [1.1] vs 1.7 [1.2]; P=.003). No significant between-group differences were observed in the incidence of hoarseness (P=.526) or dry mouth (P=.222). No acupuncture-related adverse events were observed.
In this randomized clinical trial, wrist-ankle acupuncture significantly reduced postoperative sore throat severity compared to sham acupuncture. These findings suggest that this simple, minimally invasive technique may be a safe and effective therapeutic option for managing persistent postoperative sore throat despite standard prophylactic measures.
This study was registered at Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400087964).

papers.title: From pin factory to Panchakarma: A neo-Smithian division of intelligence for AI-enabled Ayurveda.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.authors: Mathur A
papers.abstract: Ayurveda and contemporary artificial intelligence face an inverse paradox. Ayurveda has accumulated several thousand years of individualised clinical observation but remains underrepresented in the global evidence base, because it is repeatedly evaluated using a testing architecture designed for single-molecule interventions and ill-suited to individualised, integrated care. Contemporary artificial intelligence (AI), by contrast, has frameworks for extracting structure from observation but lacks domain-specific clinical data in traditional medicine. This paper argues that the two are complementary: AI applied to terminology mapping, retrospective cohort analysis from electronic medical records, signal detection in routine clinical data, and evidence synthesis across classical and contemporary sources changes the economics of evidence generation enough to make it feasible. The argument is developed through a neo-Smithian division-of-intelligence framework, adapted from earlier work, that allocates clinical tasks across AI-first, hybrid, and human-first categories on grounds respecting both the structure of Ayurvedic practice and the comparative advantages of contemporary AI. A three-layer operational architecture, comprising a data foundation, analytics pipelines, and multi-audience delivery, is set out and tested against two contrasting clinical cases, type-2 diabetes and supportive cancer care, before being mapped onto India's regulatory framework for Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani (ASU) products. The distributional question is then addressed, six risks are named, legal implications are set out, and a phased five-year roadmap closes the argument. The technology, the regulation, and the international policy environment are now sufficient; what remains is the institutional and methodological work to carry the framework into practice.
